summary: Nirmal Chandra Sinha was a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta, he was the founder director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology (1958–1987) and Centenary Professor at the University of Calcutta (1971).
Nirupam Chakma is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA at the International Buddhist College, where he was attested in 2015 studying under supervisors Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing.
Nitin Kumar Jain is an Indologist who completed his PhD at Central Sanskrit University, where he was appointed Assistant Professor in 2019.
Nivitigala Sumitta Thero is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He completed a PhD at the University of the West (2014–2023) and became Founder and CEO of Dhamma USA in 2022.
Noa Gal is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a DPhil at the University of Oxford under the supervision of Richard Gombrich, attested in 2003.

Noa Ronkin specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Wolfson College and the University of Oxford (D.Phil. 2003) under Richard Gombrich and Shlomo Biderman, she served as a Lecturer and Research Fellow at Stanford University in 2005.
Noah Avigan is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. Attested as a graduate student at Yale University in 2026, he held a post in Religious Studies there.

Noboru Karashima was a historian and Indologist who earned his degrees, including a Litt.D. (1993), at the University of Tokyo. He held posts there (1964–1994, Professor Emeritus 1981–1994) and served as Professor at Taisho University (~1994–2008).

Noboru Miyata was a scholar of religious studies, Japanology, and folklore history. Educated at Tokyo University of Education and the University of Tsukuba, he taught at Tokyo Gakugei University (~1970–1979) and was Professor of Folklore at Tsukuba (~1979–1999).
Noboru Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who held a post at the University of Tokyo, attested in 1990, and served as a professor at Mejiro University, attested in 2015.

Nobuchiyo Kotani is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied at Kyoto and Otani universities. He served as Professor at Otani University (~1980–2014) and President of Otani University Junior College (~1998–2004).

Nobuhiko Kobayashi is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University. He held academic posts at the University of Toronto (attested 1969), Kyoto University (attested 1979), and Taisho University (attested 2026).

Nobuhiro Ota is a historian and Indologist who completed his undergraduate and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He has served on the faculty at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies since 2002, becoming professor in 2021.
Nobukatsu Komai is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a research student at Taisho University and served as a full-time researcher at Chisan Denpōin, attested in 2014.
Nobumasa Hibi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Rissho University from ~1955 to 1959 and later served as an assistant professor there, attested in 1972.

Tensho (Nobumasa) Miyazaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Tokyo (~2002–2009) and later held research and teaching posts at Toyo, Tokyo, and Tokyo Agriculture universities.

Nobumi Iyanaga is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who attended the École Pratique des Hautes Études until 1969. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2003) and the École française d'Extrême-Orient Tokyo Centre (2008–2014).
Nobuo Otsuka is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework and served as a researcher at Taisho University, attested in 1995.

Nobuyoshi Yamabe is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Osaka, Otani, and Yale (PhD 1999), he served as Associate Professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (1996), Professor at Tokyo University of Agriculture (2003), and Professor at Waseda (2015).

Nobuyuki Kaji is a philosopher and Sinologist educated at Kyoto and Tohoku universities. He served as professor at Osaka University (1984–1998), president of Koshien Junior College (1998–1999), and special invited professor at Ritsumeikan University (2008–2015).
